CANADA SELF-EMPLOYED TAX SET-ASIDE · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

How much of what you earn should you set aside for tax?

Enter your business revenue and expenses. You get CPP (both halves), federal income tax, a provincial estimate, and the share of every invoice to put away.

Written from the published CRA tables for 2025 and 2026 without a live lookup. CRA decides. Not tax advice.

Enter your revenue, then click Calculate.

What it does, and what it leaves to you

    
    
      
  • Covers: CPP and CPP2 on net self-employment income, the CPP deduction and credit, federal brackets and basic personal amount, a flat provincial estimate, and flags for instalments and GST/HST registration.
    • 
      
  • Not decided: real provincial brackets and credits (Quebec has its own QPP and tax), other income, RRSP and other deductions, the home-office and vehicle rules, GST/HST amounts, and whether you must pay instalments. CRA or your accountant decide these.
    • 
    

  


  

    
Common questions

    
How much of my self-employed income should I set aside for tax in Canada?

    
A common planning range is 25% to 35% of profit once you add CPP, federal and provincial tax. Use your revenue and expenses here for a number built from the actual tables.

    
How much CPP do self-employed people pay?

    
You pay both halves: 11.9% of net self-employment earnings between $3,500 and the year's maximum pensionable earnings, plus 8% on earnings between that and the second ceiling (CPP2).

    
Do I have to pay tax quarterly?

    
If you owe more than $3,000 in the current year and also did in either of the two years before, CRA expects instalments on March 15, June 15, September 15 and December 15.

    
When must I register for GST/HST?

    
When your taxable sales pass $30,000 over four consecutive calendar quarters. GST/HST you collect is not your income, so keep it out of your set-aside.

    
Is my data uploaded anywhere?

    
No. Everything is calculated in your browser and nothing is sent.

Everything runs in your browser. Your answers are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (analysis_run, example_loaded, summary_downloaded) are counted only in local storage on your device, never with any of your data, and are switched off by Do Not Track.
